finding.claim: /checkout charges a total computed entirely from client-supplied price and qty, with no catalog lookup or server-side validation. A caller can pay an arbitrary amount, or a negative amount if payments.charge accepts negatives.

trace.note: total = sum of client i.price * i.qty, no validation

finding.guards_checked: No catalog lookup, no sign/finite/integer check on price or qty, no upper bound, no comparison with server price. Sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13) uses catalog price, so the fix exists but was not applied here. Route auth middleware is outside this repo and unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js. cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup, sign, finiteness, integer, or upper-bound check. cart.js:6 passes that total straight to req.payments.charge with no comparison to a server-side price. The sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) uses req.catalog.price(i.sku) and Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)), so the fix exists but is not applied to /checkout. Auth middleware (req.user) and payments.charge's handling of negative amounts are outside this directory and unverified.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: cart.js:5 computes the total from client price and qty, and cart.js:6 charges it with no validation, so any authenticated user who can reach the route can pay an arbitrary amount (e.g. price 0.01). The negative-amount sub-claim depends on payments.charge, which is not in this repo, so it is unverified and should be dropped or qualified; the core underpricing claim does not depend on it.

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 can charge NaN. A missing or non-numeric qty, or a catalog price of undefined for an unknown SKU, makes total NaN, and it is charged without a finiteness check. Impact depends on payments.charge, which is not in this repo.

trace.note: p = await req.catalog.price(i.sku); may be undefined for unknown SKU
Math.max(1, Math.floor(qty)) yields NaN for missing or non-numeric qty; p*qty then NaN
charge issued with total, which may be NaN
response returns charged: null for NaN

finding.guards_checked: Math.max(1,...) blocks zero and negative qty but not NaN. No Number.isFinite or total>0 check before charge. Whether payments.charge rejects, coerces to 0, or books a bad record is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:14 Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) does not handle NaN (Math.floor(undefined) and Math.max(1, NaN) both yield NaN), and there is no Number.isFinite or total > 0 check between line 13 and the charge at line 16. The trace matches the file: line 12 loops over client items, line 13 awaits the catalog price, line 14 is the multiplication, line 16 is the charge, and line 17 serializes NaN as null.
verdict.reason: NaN reaches payments.charge at cart.js:16 with no finiteness check at cart.js:14-16, so the code-level claim holds. The attacker needs only to send a request with a missing qty or unknown sku, which affects their own charge (req.user.id); whether that becomes a real financial loss depends on payments.charge, which is not in this repo, so the severity is modest and not verified.
